Resolves #21917

A `stores` replacement that throws no longer leaves a provider's borrowers on a destroyed store. `Provider#beforeSetStores` destroyed the owned stores a new map replaced before building that map. So a malformed later descriptor, or a store that rejected its config, left every child provider resolving a destroyed store, while the successors built before the throw stayed registered and owned. The map now builds first:
- An explicit id it reuses is released from the instance and store registries, not destroyed.
- The replaced stores retire only once every successor stands.
- A throw destroys the successors and any store that took its id while its configs applied, nothing else. It then gives released stores their registrations back, restores the generation, and rethrows.

Evidence: L2 (unit specs, red before the change, the full unit suite green after, plus a mutation check) → L2 required (provider bookkeeping, nothing rendered).

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `test/playwright/unit/state/ProviderRejectedStoresReplacement.spec.mjs`. After `{plan, invalid: null}`, after `{plan, typo: 'oops', invalid: null}`, and after a store whose `rejects` config throws while its configs apply, the child provider still resolves the original store. It is not destroyed, holds its one record, and both registries return it. |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: the same spec. The `plan` successor built before the throw (`<root>__plan__1`) and the half-built `audit` store (`<root>__audit__1`) are in neither registry. A corrected replacement then succeeds, its store resolves through the child, and the original retires. |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: `Provider.spec.mjs` keeps its explicit-id reuse, implicit-generation and passed-in-survival replacement tests green; the full unit suite passes 8571, 2 skipped. |

## Deltas from ticket

- The explicit-id case fails coherently too. When the failed map reuses the original's explicit id, the original takes its registrations back, and a corrected retry under the same id succeeds (third test).
- The rollback destroys a half-built store only when the failed build changed who holds its id. An unrelated store that already held a failed descriptor's id survives (fourth test). With that holder check removed, the fourth test fails in a scratch worktree and the other three pass.
- A failed map leaves the id generation where it was, so a corrected retry gets the ids the failed attempt would have used.
- Only an instance the build made counts as its successor. An entry `beforeSetInstance` passes through as it is (a string, say) is neither owned nor destroyed. Every rollback teardown frees its registrations even when its `destroy()` throws, so the restore always completes and the original error surfaces. This is the mixed map from Emmy's review (fifth test).

## Test Evidence

Before the change, the first three tests of the new spec fail at `original.isDestroyed`, and the mixed-map test fails at c645ffd740 with "store.destroy is not a function". At cf086e7631, `npm run test-unit` passes 8572 (2 skipped).

None: the change is provider bookkeeping, covered by unit specs in CI.
